scope: git diff 5c0877b..HEAD on 005-announcing-a-version-published; lenses correctness, spec-compliance, security

findings.claim: publish() leaves the in-memory instance reporting a publication that was rolled back when Acceptance.subject_of() raises RecordError.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/models.py publish(): self.status/published_at/html/publisher are assigned before Acceptance.subject_of(publisher) is called (it raises RecordError for a user with no pk). The atomic block rolls the database back, but the instance is not restored.
findings.reproduction: v2 = VersionFactory(document=v.document, markdown='other'); v2.publish(publisher=User(username='x')) raises RecordError; afterwards v2.status == 'current' and v2.published_at is set in memory, while v2.refresh_from_db() gives status 'draft'. No signal is sent (correct). Not reachable from the admin (request.user is saved), only from code passing an unsaved user.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the subject before mutating: move `subject = '' if publisher is None else Acceptance.subject_of(publisher)` above the first assignment to self (or above the supersede update) and assign it later.

notes: Migration 0005_version_publisher.py uses single quotes and unwrapped long lines (generated output, not run through the formatter).

Probes run on a /tmp copy, each reverted after: removing publisher from PUBLISHED_FROZEN_FIELDS, sending directly instead of on_commit, and send instead of send_robust each fail a test; removing the subject whitespace collapse fails the line-break subject test. The guards are real.
